rubric.name: reviewed-vocabulary-growth plan r3 (new panel after a below-quorum round)
criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, the software does not demonstrably do what it claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.
For this plan, a concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, a phase cannot be specified, implemented or tested as written, or the milestone would not do what its goal claims.

This is a new panel run over plan r3. Round 1 read r1 and has a panel result; round 2 read r2 and reached no quorum, so it has none. Their records are .gnd-planning/milestones/reviewed-vocabulary-growth/evidence/plan-review-r1/disposition.md and .gnd-planning/milestones/reviewed-vocabulary-growth/evidence/plan-review-r2/disposition.md and may be read for context. In the plan, (p1) marks a repair from round 1, (s2) a repair from one of the two single reviews of round 2, and (m) a change by the author that no reviewer asked for. Do not restate a concern that r3 repairs. Report an earlier concern again only if its repair is wrong or incomplete, and say which.

Is each (p1) and (s2) repair correct against the repository at this checkout and consistent with the rest of the plan? In particular: obligations H30 to H36 and the corrected H13 and H27 (read the cited lines in src/gnd, tests and .codex/skills/process-phase/references/project.md before reporting a mismatch); criteria VG1-C7, VG1-C8, VG3-C2, VG3-C3, VG3-C5, VG3-C8, VG3-C9, VG3-C10 and VG4-C3; and the D2 (b) readings of VG2 and VG5.

D13 proposes that an included element of an unattended root is exempt from U2 to U7, and from U8 only when its status is confirmed, with the root's pin as the statement of review and the remaining trust named as a limit in section 6. D14 proposes that a span an included element carries is still re-hashed and counted when it names a document the root declares, and ignored otherwise. Are both proposals implementable and testable as written, do they agree with src/gnd/model/_unattended.py, src/gnd/model/_includes.py and src/gnd/commands/checking.py, and do they keep the output of an unattended include root that validates today (H30)? Is anything a host could still carry through an include left unstated?

Section 2 now writes the first-document rule of D4 (a) on the file: every section of the root other than version, model_id, source and includes is absent or empty. Does that leave any way for a root with a claim of its own to validate with no source document, and does it refuse anything it should admit? Check it against src/gnd/schema/orm-meta.schema.json and src/gnd/model/_includes.py.
Do sections 0, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 10 still agree with each other after the repairs? Name any criterion, decision, home or lane that r2 left stale, contradictory or untestable.

The VG1 draft spec at .gnd-planning/milestones/reviewed-vocabulary-growth/notes/phase-VG1-spec.md may be read for context; a concern about it must still cite the plan file and name the spec line in the observation.
Every concern's evidence must cite the plan file, with a verbatim quotation of the plan text the concern is about.
